Source batch ~1,068 g raw batter, scaled to 1 kg baked cake (92% yield).

1. Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease and line two 8-inch tins. | 2. Stir milk with vinegar and rest a few minutes so it thickens slightly. | 3. Whisk in sugar, oil and vanilla until the sugar mostly dissolves. | 4. Sift flour, cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda and salt into the bowl and mix just until smooth. | 5. Divide between the tins and bake 20–22 minutes, until the tops spring back. Cool fully before filling or frosting.

Source batch ~1,165 g raw batter. Hot coffee/water is counted in the batter but not costed in her original sheet; this adapted version costs a small amount of brewed coffee / hot water at an estimated price. Light + cane sugar are entered as granulated sugar, matching her sheet.

1. Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease and line two 8-inch tins. | 2. Mix milk and vinegar; rest 5 minutes. | 3. Whisk in both sugars (here, all granulated), oil and vanilla. | 4. Sift flour, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt; fold into the wet mix until smooth. | 5. Stir in hot coffee or boiling water to bloom the cocoa, split between tins, and bake 25–30 minutes. Cool completely.

Source batch ~1,198 g raw batter, scaled to 1 kg. Her cream cheese frosting is a separate recipe.

1. Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease and line two 8-inch tins. | 2. Combine milk, yogurt and vinegar; rest until slightly curdled. | 3. Whisk in oil, sugar, vanilla and red gel colour. | 4. Sift flour, cocoa, cornstarch, baking soda and salt; mix in just until smooth. | 5. Bake 30–40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool fully, then level the tops before frosting.

Taken from the coconut sponge in her Mango Coconut Cake. Batch ~1,012 g, scaled to 1 kg. Lemon juice in the source is swapped for white vinegar, matching her existing recipe.

1. Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease and line two 8-inch tins. | 2. Stir milk, vinegar (or lemon juice) and yogurt; rest briefly. | 3. Whisk in oil, sugar and vanilla, then stir through desiccated coconut. | 4. Sift flour, cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda and salt; mix until just smooth. | 5. Bake 25–30 minutes until springy. Cool, then level before filling.

Egg whites are about 5 per kg; costed at the whole-egg price (slightly high).

1. Warm egg whites with the sugar over a gentle water bath, stirring until the sugar dissolves and the mix is hot to the touch. | 2. Whip to a glossy, cool meringue. | 3. Beat in soft butter a little at a time, then vanilla and salt, until smooth and silky. | 4. If it looks curdled, keep beating; if too soft, chill briefly and beat again.
